It should be noted that the speed of Nepal's recovery will not only depend on the amount of

external financing received. Other key factors include the extent to which Nepal's absorptive

capacity is increased by addressing implementation bottlenecks, as well as effective

coordination among donors.

financial markets, the main external risks to the outlook stem from a slowdown in host

countries for Nepali workers (especially in oil-exporting countries, e.g., the GCC countries

and Malaysia), and a potential slower-than-anticipated recovery in India, which is Nepal's

largest trading partner. Domestic risks are related to long-standing vulnerabilities in the

financial sector, as identified in the 2014 FSAP, and political instability which could

undermine confidence and delay economic reforms.
